02-01.title: Clark Gable
02-01.description: The 'King of Hollywood' whose suave magnetism and roguish charm defined the golden age of cinema, immortalized as Rhett Butler in Gone with the Wind.

02-01.title: Boris Yeltsin
02-01.description: First President of the Russian Federation who stood on a tank in 1991 to face down a coup and presided over the Soviet Union's dramatic dissolution.

02-01.title: Harry Styles
02-01.description: British pop superstar who parlayed One Direction fame into a critically acclaimed solo career, winning Grammys and selling out stadiums worldwide.

02-01.title: The Beatles Top U.S. Charts
02-01.description: I Want to Hold Your Hand reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100, kicking off seven consecutive weeks at the top and igniting American Beatlemania.

02-01.title: Myanmar Military Coup
02-01.description: The Tatmadaw seized power and detained democratically elected leader Aung San Suu Kyi, triggering mass protests and international condemnation.

02-01.title: Dookie — Green Day
02-01.description: Green Day's punk-pop breakthrough unleashed anthems like Basket Case and Longview on an unsuspecting world, winning the Grammy for Best Alternative Album.

02-01.title: Sound City
02-01.description: Dave Grohl's loving documentary about Sound City Studios, the legendary Hollywood recording space where Nirvana made Nevermind, features testimony from rock royalty.

02-02.title: James Joyce
02-02.description: Irish literary modernist whose stream-of-consciousness masterwork Ulysses and the experimental Finnegans Wake permanently altered the course of the novel.

02-02.title: Shakira
02-02.description: Colombian superstar whose irresistible blend of Latin pop, rock, and belly dance moves made her one of the best-selling musical artists of all time.

02-02.title: Farrah Fawcett
02-02.description: Iconic actress and model whose 1976 red swimsuit poster became the best-selling poster in history and her feathered hair sparked a global style trend.

02-02.title: Battle of Stalingrad Ends
02-02.description: German Field Marshal Paulus surrendered the remnants of the Sixth Army at Stalingrad, marking the catastrophic turning point of World War II on the Eastern Front.

02-02.title: Groundhog Day Tradition
02-02.description: Punxsutawney Phil made his first official weather prediction in Pennsylvania, beginning a folklore tradition that persists every February 2nd to this day.

02-02.title: A Trick of the Tail — Genesis
02-02.description: Genesis released their first album with Phil Collins on lead vocals after Peter Gabriel's departure, silencing doubters with an ambitious and commercially successful prog-rock statement.

02-02.title: Groundhog Day
02-02.description: Bill Murray's endlessly rewatchable philosophical comedy about a weatherman trapped in a time loop became one of the most beloved films of its decade.

02-03.title: Felix Mendelssohn
02-03.description: German Romantic composer and child prodigy whose Wedding March, Songs Without Words, and Violin Concerto remain cornerstones of the classical repertoire.

02-03.title: Norman Rockwell
02-03.description: American illustrator whose warm, detail-rich Saturday Evening Post covers captured small-town life and ideals with such precision they became the face of 20th-century America.

02-03.title: Gertrude Stein
02-03.description: Avant-garde American writer and art collector who presided over a legendary Paris salon, championing Picasso and coining the phrase 'a rose is a rose is a rose.'

02-03.title: The Day the Music Died
02-03.description: Rock pioneers Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens, and The Big Bopper perished in a plane crash near Clear Lake, Iowa, in a tragedy later immortalized in Don McLean's American Pie.

02-03.title: Luna 9 Moon Landing
02-03.description: The Soviet Union's Luna 9 spacecraft became the first to achieve a soft landing on the Moon and transmit photographs directly from the lunar surface.

02-03.title: American Pie — Don McLean
02-03.description: Don McLean's eight-minute elegy for Buddy Holly and the loss of rock and roll innocence became one of the most analyzed and beloved songs in American music history.

02-03.title: The Buddy Holly Story
02-03.description: Gary Busey's Oscar-nominated portrayal of the rock and roll pioneer captures his meteoric rise and the tragic early end to a revolutionary musical life.

02-04.title: Rosa Parks
02-04.description: Civil rights activist whose quiet refusal to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama, in 1955 ignited the modern civil rights movement in America.

02-04.title: Charles Lindbergh
02-04.description: Aviator who became the first person to fly solo and nonstop across the Atlantic Ocean in 1927, completing the 33-hour journey from New York to Paris in the Spirit of St. Louis.

02-04.title: Alice Cooper
02-04.description: The Godfather of Shock Rock who pioneered theatrical heavy metal, fusing horror-film stagecraft with hard rock anthems like School's Out and Poison.

02-04.title: Facebook Founded
02-04.description: Mark Zuckerberg and Eduardo Saverin launched Facebook from a Harvard dorm room, a social network that would grow to connect more than three billion people worldwide.

02-04.title: Fleetwood Mac Releases Rumours
02-04.description: Recorded amid the romantic collapse of two band couples, Rumours became one of the best-selling albums of all time, spending 31 weeks at number one in the US.

02-04.title: Stayin' Alive — Bee Gees
02-04.description: The Bee Gees' falsetto-driven disco anthem hit number one on the Billboard Hot 100 and became the definitive soundtrack of the Saturday Night Fever era.

02-04.title: Saturday Night Fever
02-04.description: John Travolta's electrifying dancing in Brooklyn's disco underworld made this film a cultural phenomenon and the Bee Gees' soundtrack one of the best-selling of all time.

02-05.title: Cristiano Ronaldo
02-05.description: Portuguese soccer superstar who has scored more international goals than any player in history, winning five Ballon d'Or awards and Champions League titles at multiple clubs.

02-05.title: Neymar
02-05.description: Brazilian football wizard celebrated for his extraordinary dribbling and flamboyant skill, who became the world's most expensive player when PSG signed him for €222 million.

02-05.title: Bobby Brown
02-05.description: New Jack Swing pioneer whose solo debut Don't Be Cruel produced a string of chart-toppers and helped define the sound of late 1980s R&B.

02-05.title: Welcome Stranger Gold Nugget Found
02-05.description: Gold prospectors in Moliagul, Victoria, Australia, unearthed the Welcome Stranger, the largest alluvial gold nugget ever found, weighing an astonishing 72 kilograms.

02-05.title: Bakelite Announced
02-05.description: Belgian chemist Leo Baekeland unveiled Bakelite, the first fully synthetic plastic, launching the modern plastics industry and transforming manufacturing worldwide.

02-05.title: Don't Be Cruel — Bobby Brown
02-05.description: Bobby Brown's second album became one of the best-selling R&B records of the 1980s, spawning five top-ten singles and defining the New Jack Swing movement.

02-05.title: Fast Times at Ridgemont High
02-05.description: Amy Heckerling's sharply observed coming-of-age comedy set in a California mall introduced Sean Penn's stoner icon Jeff Spicoli and launched several major careers.

02-06.title: Bob Marley
02-06.description: Jamaican reggae legend who spread Rastafarian philosophy and infectious rhythms worldwide, becoming a global symbol of peace, justice, and liberation.

02-06.title: Ronald Reagan
02-06.description: 40th President of the United States, former actor turned conservative icon, who oversaw a massive peacetime military build-up credited with hastening the end of the Cold War.

02-06.title: Babe Ruth
02-06.description: Baseball's greatest legend, whose prodigious home-run hitting in the 1920s transformed the game and whose records and mythology have never truly been surpassed.

02-06.title: Queen Elizabeth II Accedes to the Throne
02-06.description: Upon the death of her father George VI, Princess Elizabeth became Queen while staying at Treetops Hotel in Kenya, beginning the longest reign in British history.

02-06.title: Munich Air Disaster
02-06.description: A plane carrying Manchester United's young squad, the Busby Babes, crashed on takeoff in Munich, killing eight players and devastating English football.

02-06.title: Legend — Bob Marley & the Wailers
02-06.description: This posthumous greatest-hits collection became the best-selling reggae album of all time, introducing generations to the uplifting sounds and message of Bob Marley.

02-06.title: This Is Spinal Tap
02-06.description: Rob Reiner's groundbreaking mockumentary about the world's loudest band pioneered the genre and delivered comedy so authentic it was mistaken for a real documentary.

02-07.title: Charles Dickens
02-07.description: Victorian England's greatest novelist, who drew on his own childhood poverty to create unforgettable characters in Oliver Twist, A Tale of Two Cities, and Great Expectations.

02-07.title: Laura Ingalls Wilder
02-07.description: American author whose beloved Little House on the Prairie series chronicled her pioneering childhood on the American frontier and shaped generations of young readers.

02-07.title: Chris Rock
02-07.description: Stand-up comedian and filmmaker widely regarded as one of the greatest comics of his generation, known for incisive social commentary delivered with razor-sharp wit.

02-07.title: Beatles Arrive in America
02-07.description: The Fab Four landed at John F. Kennedy Airport to a screaming mob of fans, beginning the British Invasion that would permanently reshape American popular music.

02-07.title: New Madrid Earthquake
02-07.description: The most violent quake in the New Madrid series struck Missouri with such ferocity it made the Mississippi River run backward for several hours.

02-07.title: The Kick Inside — Kate Bush
02-07.description: Kate Bush's extraordinary debut album, built around the career-launching single Wuthering Heights, announced one of rock's most distinctive and original voices.

02-07.title: The Lego Movie
02-07.description: Phil Lord and Christopher Miller's wildly inventive animated comedy surprised critics and audiences with its sharp meta-humor and an unexpectedly heartfelt story about creativity.

02-08.title: Jules Verne
02-08.description: French author who pioneered science fiction with prophetic novels like Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea and Around the World in Eighty Days, inspiring generations of explorers and scientists.

02-08.title: Jack Lemmon
02-08.description: Versatile Hollywood star who won two Academy Awards and brought comic and dramatic brilliance to classics like Some Like It Hot and The Apartment.

02-08.title: John Williams
02-08.description: The most successful film composer of all time, whose iconic scores for Star Wars, Jaws, Schindler's List, and Indiana Jones are woven into the fabric of popular culture.

02-08.title: Boy Scouts of America Founded
02-08.description: William Dickson Boyce incorporated the Boy Scouts of America in Washington, D.C., establishing one of the largest youth organizations in American history.

02-08.title: Confederacy Formed
02-08.description: Delegates from six seceded Southern states convened in Montgomery, Alabama, and formally established the Confederate States of America, setting the stage for the Civil War.

02-08.title: Star Wars — Original Motion Picture Soundtrack
02-08.description: John Williams' sweeping orchestral score for George Lucas's space epic restored the full symphonic sound to Hollywood and won the Academy Award for Best Original Score.

02-08.title: The Hateful Eight
02-08.description: Quentin Tarantino's snow-bound mystery thriller locked eight strangers in a Wyoming haberdashery and slowly, savagely revealed who among them was a killer.

02-09.title: Carole King
02-09.description: Singer-songwriter who transformed American pop from the Brill Building era to the singer-songwriter revolution, releasing the landmark album Tapestry in 1971.

02-09.title: Joe Pesci
02-09.description: Intense character actor whose explosive performances in Raging Bull and Goodfellas earned him an Academy Award and cemented his status as a master of menace.

02-09.title: Mia Farrow
02-09.description: Acclaimed actress whose haunting performance in Rosemary's Baby established her as a major Hollywood talent and whose decades of humanitarian work have defined her legacy.

02-09.title: Beatles on The Ed Sullivan Show
02-09.description: An estimated 73 million Americans watched the Beatles perform on The Ed Sullivan Show, the most watched television broadcast in U.S. history to that point.

02-09.title: Tom Hiddleston Born
02-09.description: English actor celebrated for his charismatic portrayal of Loki across the Marvel Cinematic Universe, bringing wit and depth to one of superhero fiction's greatest antiheroes.

02-09.title: Tapestry — Carole King
02-09.description: Carole King's intimate masterwork spent 15 weeks at number one and won four Grammy Awards, making it one of the best-selling albums by a female artist in history.

02-09.title: Rosemary's Baby
02-09.description: Roman Polanski's masterful psychological horror film, with Mia Farrow as a pregnant woman who suspects her neighbors are Satanists, remains one of cinema's most chilling works.

02-10.title: Bertolt Brecht
02-10.description: German playwright and poet whose Threepenny Opera and epic theatre techniques deliberately broke illusions to provoke political thought in audiences.

02-10.title: Shirley Temple
02-10.description: Curly-haired child star who became America's biggest box-office draw during the Depression, lifting spirits with films like Bright Eyes before transitioning to a diplomatic career.

02-10.title: Emma Roberts
02-10.description: American actress celebrated for her versatile work across Ryan Murphy's American Horror Story franchise and a range of film and television projects.

02-10.title: Deep Blue Defeats Kasparov
02-10.description: IBM's Deep Blue became the first computer program to win a chess game against a reigning world champion, Garry Kasparov, in a milestone for artificial intelligence.

02-10.title: Treaty of Paris Ends Seven Years' War
02-10.description: Britain, France, Spain, and Portugal signed the Treaty of Paris, ending the Seven Years' War and reshaping colonial possessions across North America, the Caribbean, and India.

02-10.title: Tapestry — Carole King
02-10.description: Carole King released her iconic singer-songwriter landmark on this date, featuring You've Got a Friend and It's Too Late, and it went on to sell over 25 million copies.

02-10.title: Chitty Chitty Bang Bang
02-10.description: This spectacular musical fantasy, based on Ian Fleming's children's novel and featuring Dick Van Dyke, remains a beloved family film with an unforgettably catchy title song.

02-11.title: Thomas Edison
02-11.description: America's greatest inventor, whose prodigious creativity produced the phonograph, the practical incandescent light bulb, and over 1,000 other patents that shaped the modern world.

02-11.title: Jennifer Aniston
02-11.description: Beloved actress whose decade-long role as Rachel Green on Friends made her an international icon, and whose subsequent film career proved her enduring comedic and dramatic range.

02-11.title: Sheryl Crow
02-11.description: Rock singer-songwriter who burst onto the scene with All I Wanna Do and went on to collect nine Grammy Awards across a career of melodic, socially aware rock.

02-11.title: Nelson Mandela Released
02-11.description: After 27 years imprisoned by the apartheid government, Nelson Mandela walked free from Victor Verster Prison, a moment that signaled the beginning of South Africa's transition to democracy.

02-11.title: First Visions of Lourdes
02-11.description: Bernadette Soubirous reported the first of eighteen visions of the Virgin Mary in a grotto near Lourdes, France, transforming the town into one of the world's most visited pilgrimage sites.

02-11.title: Tuesday Night Music Club — Sheryl Crow
02-11.description: Sheryl Crow's debut album, recorded informally with a group of musician friends, produced the Grammy-winning All I Wanna Do and established her as rock's freshest new voice.

02-11.title: Silence of the Lambs
02-11.description: Jonathan Demme's Oscar-sweeping psychological thriller paired FBI trainee Jodie Foster against the brilliantly terrifying Anthony Hopkins as Hannibal Lecter in a cat-and-mouse masterpiece.

02-12.title: Abraham Lincoln
02-12.description: 16th President of the United States who guided the nation through the Civil War and issued the Emancipation Proclamation, preserving the Union and ending slavery.

02-12.title: Charles Darwin
02-12.description: English naturalist whose theory of evolution by natural selection, published in On the Origin of Species, fundamentally transformed how humanity understands life on Earth.

02-12.title: Bill Russell
02-12.description: Boston Celtics center considered the greatest winner in team sports history, who led the Celtics to 11 NBA championships in 13 seasons and revolutionized defensive basketball.

02-12.title: NAACP Founded
02-12.description: On Lincoln's 100th birthday, activists including W.E.B. Du Bois founded the NAACP in New York City, establishing the nation's oldest and largest civil rights organization.

02-12.title: Rhapsody in Blue Premieres
02-12.description: George Gershwin's genre-defying Rhapsody in Blue received its world premiere at Aeolian Hall in New York, brilliantly fusing jazz idioms with classical orchestral form.

02-12.title: Rhapsody in Blue — George Gershwin
02-12.description: Gershwin's landmark concerto-like work premiered on this very day, blending the blues and jazz scales of African-American music with the harmonic language of European Romanticism.

02-12.title: Lincoln
02-12.description: Steven Spielberg's meticulous historical drama, with Daniel Day-Lewis's towering Oscar-winning performance, illuminates Lincoln's masterful political maneuvering to pass the 13th Amendment.

02-13.title: Kim Novak
02-13.description: Luminous Hollywood actress whose mesmerizing dual performance in Alfred Hitchcock's Vertigo is widely regarded as one of the greatest in film history.

02-13.title: Robbie Williams
02-13.description: British pop superstar who left Take That to become one of the best-selling solo artists in history, famed for his charismatic performances and hits like Angels and Feel.

02-13.title: Peter Gabriel
02-13.description: Art rock pioneer and Genesis co-founder whose visionary solo career produced Sledgehammer, Biko, and the landmark World Music movement via his Real World label.

02-13.title: ASCAP Founded
02-13.description: The American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers was established in New York City to protect the rights of music creators and ensure they are compensated for public performances.

02-13.title: Bombing of Dresden Begins
02-13.description: British and American bombers began four days of devastating raids on Dresden, Germany, creating a firestorm visible for 200 miles and killing tens of thousands of civilians.

02-13.title: So — Peter Gabriel
02-13.description: Peter Gabriel's commercially triumphant fifth album contained Sledgehammer, In Your Eyes, and Big Time, bringing his experimental art-rock vision to a massive global audience.

02-13.title: Vertigo
02-13.description: Alfred Hitchcock's psychologically complex masterpiece, starring James Stewart and Kim Novak, is regularly ranked the greatest film ever made by critics worldwide.

02-14.title: Frederick Douglass
02-14.description: Self-educated escaped slave who became the most influential African-American abolitionist, orator, and author of the 19th century, advising President Lincoln during the Civil War.

02-14.title: Jack Benny
02-14.description: Master comedian of radio and television whose carefully crafted persona of vanity and penny-pinching made him one of the most beloved entertainers of the 20th century.

02-14.title: Simon Pegg
02-14.description: British actor, writer, and comedian whose Cornetto Trilogy with Edgar Wright—Shaun of the Dead, Hot Fuzz, and The World's End—revitalized the comedy genre.

02-14.title: St. Valentine's Day Massacre
02-14.description: Al Capone's gunmen, disguised as police officers, executed seven members of Bugs Moran's gang in a Chicago garage, shocking even crime-hardened America.

02-14.title: Galileo Born
02-14.description: Galileo Galilei was born in Pisa, Tuscany, and would grow up to father modern observational astronomy, confirm heliocentrism, and lay the groundwork for classical mechanics.

02-14.title: Respect — Aretha Franklin
02-14.description: Aretha Franklin recorded her electrifying reinterpretation of Otis Redding's Respect at Atlantic Records, transforming a man's plea into an anthem of feminine and civil rights empowerment.

02-14.title: Shaun of the Dead
02-14.description: Edgar Wright's brilliantly crafted romantic zombie comedy introduced the world to the affectionate and wickedly funny horror parodies of the Wright-Pegg-Frost creative partnership.

02-15.title: Galileo Galilei
02-15.description: Italian astronomer and physicist who championed heliocentrism through his telescopic observations, faced the Inquisition for his beliefs, and laid the foundations of modern physics.

02-15.title: Jane Seymour
02-15.description: British-American actress who gained international recognition as the psychic Solitaire in Live and Let Die and later starred in the long-running period drama Dr. Quinn.

02-15.title: Ernest Shackleton
02-15.description: Irish-born Antarctic explorer who led the Endurance expedition and famously kept all 27 of his men alive after their ship was crushed by pack ice in one of history's greatest survival stories.

02-15.title: Fall of Singapore
02-15.description: British General Percival surrendered to Japanese forces at Singapore, with 80,000 Allied troops taken prisoner in the largest British military capitulation in history.

02-15.title: Canada Adopts Maple Leaf Flag
02-15.description: After a heated national debate, Canada officially replaced the Red Ensign with the now-iconic red and white Maple Leaf flag, giving the nation a distinct symbol of identity.

02-15.title: Meet the Beatles! — The Beatles
02-15.description: The Beatles' first US album shot to number one on this date, becoming the fastest-selling album in Capitol Records history and cementing the British Invasion.

02-15.title: Cinderella
02-15.description: Disney's animated fairy-tale masterpiece breathed new life into the struggling studio and ushered in the second golden age of Disney animation with its enduring magic.

02-16.title: The Weeknd
02-16.description: Canadian R&B phenomenon Abel Tesfaye who redefined modern pop with his dark, cinematic sound on albums Trilogy, Beauty Behind the Madness, and After Hours.

02-16.title: Sonny Bono
02-16.description: Singer, songwriter, and half of the iconic Sonny and Cher duo who later reinvented himself as Mayor of Palm Springs and a U.S. Congressman from California.

02-16.title: Elizabeth Olsen
02-16.description: American actress who delivered a shattering debut in the thriller Martha Marcy May Marlene and went on to portray Wanda Maximoff, the Scarlet Witch, in the Marvel universe.

02-16.title: King Tutankhamun's Tomb Opened
02-16.description: Howard Carter unsealed the inner burial chamber of Tutankhamun's tomb in the Valley of the Kings, revealing the boy pharaoh's intact sarcophagus and priceless treasures.

02-16.title: ABBA: The Movie UK Premiere
02-16.description: The Swedish pop group's concert documentary film had its UK premiere in London's Leicester Square, showcasing ABBA at the height of their global popularity.

02-16.title: Beauty Behind the Madness — The Weeknd
02-16.description: The Weeknd's mainstream breakthrough album contained Can't Feel My Face and Earned It, winning two Grammy Awards and reaching number one in multiple countries.

02-16.title: Black Panther
02-16.description: Ryan Coogler's groundbreaking Marvel epic set in the fictional African nation of Wakanda became a global cultural phenomenon and won three Academy Awards.

02-17.title: Michael Jordan
02-17.description: Widely regarded as the greatest basketball player of all time, Jordan's six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls and transcendent athletic gifts made him a global cultural icon.

02-17.title: Ed Sheeran
02-17.description: British singer-songwriter who rose from busking London's streets to become one of the best-selling musicians of the 21st century, with hits spanning pop, folk, and hip-hop.

02-17.title: Paris Hilton
02-17.description: Socialite, media personality, and DJ who became one of the first reality television stars and later emerged as a successful businesswoman and advocate for prison reform.

02-17.title: Thomas Jefferson Elected President
02-17.description: The tied Electoral College vote between Jefferson and Aaron Burr was resolved by the House of Representatives, electing Jefferson the third President of the United States.

02-17.title: Kasparov Defeats Deep Blue
02-17.description: World chess champion Garry Kasparov triumphed over IBM's Deep Blue in a six-game match, demonstrating that human intuition could still outmaneuver brute computational force.

02-17.title: Their Greatest Hits (1971–1975) — Eagles
02-17.description: Released on this date, the Eagles' compilation became one of the best-selling albums in American history with over 38 million copies sold, certified 38x Platinum.

02-17.title: Footloose
02-17.description: This energetic teen drama starring Kevin Bacon as a city kid fighting a small town's ban on dancing became a defining film of the 1980s and spawned an iconic soundtrack.

02-18.title: Toni Morrison
02-18.description: Nobel Prize-winning American novelist whose searing works—Beloved, Song of Solomon, and The Bluest Eye—confronted the legacy of slavery with devastating lyrical power.

02-18.title: Dr. Dre
02-18.description: Pioneering hip-hop producer who helped launch the careers of Snoop Dogg, Eminem, and Kendrick Lamar while creating the blueprint for West Coast gangsta rap with N.W.A.

02-18.title: Molly Ringwald
02-18.description: Actress who became the definitive face of 1980s teen cinema through her collaborations with director John Hughes in The Breakfast Club and Pretty in Pink.

02-18.title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn Published
02-18.description: Mark Twain's masterpiece about a boy and an escaped slave floating down the Mississippi River was published in the U.S., immediately sparking controversy and praise it still receives today.

02-18.title: Pluto Discovered
02-18.description: Clyde Tombaugh at the Lowell Observatory in Arizona discovered Pluto after a methodical photographic survey, adding what was long considered the ninth planet to the solar system.

02-18.title: The Chronic — Dr. Dre
02-18.description: Dr. Dre's landmark debut solo album virtually invented West Coast G-funk, featuring Snoop Dogg and spawning Nuthin' but a G Thang in a record that redefined hip-hop's sound.

02-18.title: The Breakfast Club
02-18.description: John Hughes's defining portrait of high school social hierarchies locked five students from different cliques in detention and gave voice to teenage alienation with remarkable honesty.

02-19.title: Nicolaus Copernicus
02-19.description: Polish mathematician and astronomer who formulated the heliocentric model of the solar system, triggering the Scientific Revolution and displacing Earth from the center of the cosmos.

02-19.title: Smokey Robinson
02-19.description: Motown legend and founder of The Miracles whose silky tenor and gift for romantic wordplay produced classics like Tears of a Clown and The Tracks of My Tears.

02-19.title: Millie Bobby Brown
02-19.description: English actress who shot to global fame at age twelve as Eleven in Netflix's Stranger Things, becoming the youngest person ever named to TIME's 100 Most Influential list.

02-19.title: Japanese Attack on Darwin
02-19.description: Nearly 250 Japanese aircraft launched a devastating surprise attack on Darwin, Australia, killing 243 people in the largest foreign attack ever mounted on Australian soil.

02-19.title: Huaynaputina Eruption
02-19.description: The Peruvian volcano Huaynaputina exploded in the most violent eruption in the recorded history of South America, causing famine across the northern hemisphere as far as Russia.

02-19.title: For Emma, Forever Ago — Bon Iver
02-19.description: Justin Vernon recorded this intimate, heartbroken debut alone in a Wisconsin cabin during a brutal winter, and its raw beauty became one of the most acclaimed albums of the decade.

02-19.title: The Battle of Algiers
02-19.description: Gillo Pontecorvo's neorealist masterpiece about the Algerian independence struggle, shot in a documentary style so convincing that it was actually banned in France for years.

02-20.title: Kurt Cobain
02-20.description: Nirvana's tortured genius whose abrasive guitar rock and confessional lyrics on Nevermind tore down the walls of hair metal and defined an entire generation's disillusionment.

02-20.title: Rihanna
02-20.description: Barbadian pop and R&B powerhouse who has sold over 250 million records worldwide and built a fashion and beauty empire that made her one of the world's wealthiest musicians.

02-20.title: Cindy Crawford
02-20.description: American supermodel whose mole-dotted beauty and commanding presence made her one of the most recognizable faces of the 1990s and a pioneer of the celebrity model brand.

02-20.title: John Glenn Orbits Earth
02-20.description: Astronaut John Glenn became the first American to orbit the Earth, completing three orbits in Friendship 7 and becoming a national hero during the height of the Space Race.

02-20.title: Pro-Nazi Rally at Madison Square Garden
02-20.description: The German American Bund held the largest pro-Nazi rally in U.S. history at Madison Square Garden, drawing 20,000 attendees beneath a massive banner of George Washington.

02-20.title: Nevermind — Nirvana
02-20.description: Kurt Cobain's generation-defining album sold 30 million copies and knocked Michael Jackson off the Billboard number-one spot, announcing that alternative rock had conquered pop.

02-20.title: About a Boy
02-20.description: Hugh Grant gives one of his finest performances as a shallow bachelor whose unlikely friendship with a misfit twelve-year-old teaches them both how to be human.

02-21.title: Nina Simone
02-21.description: The 'High Priestess of Soul' whose extraordinary classical training, jazz inflections, and fierce civil rights activism made her one of the most singular artists of the 20th century.

02-21.title: Kelsey Grammer
02-21.description: Emmy-winning actor who inhabited the pompous yet loveable Dr. Frasier Crane for 20 years across Cheers and Frasier, one of the longest-running characters in TV history.

02-21.title: Sophie Turner
02-21.description: English actress who grew up on screen playing Sansa Stark's journey from naive girl to formidable queen across eight seasons of HBO's Game of Thrones.

02-21.title: Battle of Verdun Begins
02-21.description: Germany launched Operation Gericht along the Meuse River, beginning the longest and most grueling battle of World War I in which France and Germany suffered nearly a million combined casualties.

02-21.title: The New Yorker Publishes First Issue
02-21.description: Harold Ross launched The New Yorker magazine in New York City, establishing the literary and cultural publication that would define American letters for the next century.

02-21.title: Little Girl Blue — Nina Simone
02-21.description: Nina Simone's debut album, recorded live over two days, showcased her remarkable fusion of jazz, gospel, classical, and blues in a voice that sounded like no one else alive.

02-21.title: Malcolm X
02-21.description: Spike Lee's sweeping epic biography starred Denzel Washington in a towering performance as the civil rights leader, illuminating his transformation from street hustler to global icon.

02-22.title: George Washington
02-22.description: Commander of the Continental Army and first President of the United States, whose principled decision to step down after two terms set the democratic precedent all successors would follow.

02-22.title: Steve Irwin
02-22.description: The Crocodile Hunter whose infectious enthusiasm for wildlife brought the wonders and dangers of the natural world into millions of homes and inspired a generation of conservationists.

02-22.title: Drew Barrymore
02-22.description: Actress who charmed the world as a child in E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, overcame well-publicized personal struggles, and reinvented herself as a beloved comedic star and producer.

02-22.title: Miracle on Ice
02-22.description: The underdog U.S. Olympic hockey team stunned the heavily favored Soviet Union 4-3 at Lake Placid in one of the most celebrated upsets in sports history.

02-22.title: Galileo's Dialogue Published
02-22.description: Ferdinando II de' Medici received the first printed copy of Galileo's Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems, the book that would land its author before the Inquisition.

02-22.title: Singin' in the Rain — Gene Kelly
02-22.description: Gene Kelly's exuberant splashing through studio rain while crooning this MGM classic gave cinema one of its most joyous and iconic moments, composed by Nacio Herb Brown.

02-22.title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
02-22.description: Steven Spielberg's tender science-fiction fable about a lonely boy's friendship with a stranded alien became the highest-grossing film in history at the time of its release.

02-23.title: George Frideric Handel
02-23.description: German-British Baroque composer whose Messiah, Water Music, and Music for the Royal Fireworks remain among the most performed orchestral works in Western music history.

02-23.title: Emily Blunt
02-23.description: British actress celebrated for her chameleonic versatility, from the wickedly calculating Emily in The Devil Wears Prada to action hero in Edge of Tomorrow and Oppenheimer.

02-23.title: Dakota Fanning
02-23.description: Child prodigy actress who debuted opposite Sean Penn in I Am Sam at age seven and grew into a respected adult performer across drama, thriller, and fantasy genres.

02-23.title: Gutenberg Bible Published
02-23.description: Johannes Gutenberg completed his revolutionary 42-line Bible, the first major Western book printed with movable type, launching the print revolution that transformed civilization.

02-23.title: Iwo Jima Flag Raising
02-23.description: U.S. Marines raised the American flag atop Mount Suribachi on Iwo Jima; the photograph taken seconds later became one of the most reproduced images in history.

02-23.title: Penny Lane / Strawberry Fields Forever — The Beatles
02-23.description: The Beatles premiered the music videos for these two masterpieces on American Bandstand, a double-A-side single considered among the greatest recordings of the rock era.

02-23.title: The Messiah
02-23.description: Roberto Rossellini's reverent biographical film about the life of Jesus Christ premiered at this time, capturing the story with his characteristic neorealist directorial approach.

02-24.title: Floyd Mayweather Jr.
02-24.description: Undefeated professional boxer who retired with a 50-0 record, claiming world titles in five weight divisions and earning his reputation as the pound-for-pound greatest defensive boxer ever.

02-24.title: Daniel Kaluuya
02-24.description: British actor who won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for Judas and the Black Messiah and delivered a career-defining lead performance in Get Out.

02-24.title: Steve Jobs
02-24.description: Apple co-founder and visionary CEO whose perfectionist design ethos and revolutionary products—the Mac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad—permanently transformed personal technology.

02-24.title: Battle of Los Angeles
02-24.description: A false alarm triggered a massive anti-aircraft barrage over Los Angeles as jittery gunners opened fire on what turned out to be weather balloons and nerves after Pearl Harbor.

02-24.title: Juan Perón Elected President
02-24.description: Colonel Juan Perón was elected President of Argentina in a watershed election that launched the populist Peronist movement still shaping Argentine politics today.

02-24.title: Get Out Soundtrack
02-24.description: Michael Abels' dissonant, Swahili-chanting score for Jordan Peele's debut horror film was a revelation, weaving African musical traditions into a deeply unsettling psychological tapestry.

02-24.title: Get Out
02-24.description: Jordan Peele's debut feature used the conventions of the horror genre to deliver a chilling and pointed social satire about racism in liberal America, winning the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay.

02-25.title: George Harrison
02-25.description: The 'quiet Beatle' whose sitar explorations widened rock's vocabulary, and whose masterful post-Beatles triple album All Things Must Pass proved he had been the hidden genius all along.

02-25.title: Sean Astin
02-25.description: Actor beloved for his roles as Mikey in The Goonies, the determined Rudy, and the fiercely loyal Samwise Gamgee in Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings trilogy.

02-25.title: Enrico Caruso
02-25.description: The most celebrated tenor of the early 20th century, whose powerful voice and early phonograph recordings made him the first great recording star and opened opera to mass audiences.

02-25.title: Hiram Revels Sworn into U.S. Senate
02-25.description: Hiram Rhodes Revels of Mississippi was sworn in as the first African American to serve in the United States Senate, taking the very seat once held by Jefferson Davis.

02-25.title: Samuel Colt Patents His Revolver
02-25.description: Samuel Colt received a U.S. patent for his revolutionary revolving-cylinder firearm, a weapon that would transform warfare, law enforcement, and the mythology of the American West.

02-25.title: All Things Must Pass — George Harrison
02-25.description: George Harrison's stunning post-Beatles triple album, produced by Phil Spector, featured My Sweet Lord and What Is Life, vindicating years of creative suppression within the Fab Four.

02-25.title: The Goonies
02-25.description: Steven Spielberg's adventure comedy, starring Sean Astin and a band of kids on a treasure hunt to save their neighborhood, became one of the most beloved family films of the 1980s.

02-26.title: Victor Hugo
02-26.description: France's greatest Romantic writer, whose towering novels Les Misérables and The Hunchback of Notre-Dame combined social realism with soaring moral ambition to demand justice for the poor.

02-26.title: Fats Domino
02-26.description: New Orleans rock and roll pioneer whose rolling piano style and jovial vocals on Blueberry Hill and Ain't That a Shame sold over 65 million records and shaped early rock.

02-26.title: Johnny Cash
02-26.description: The Man in Black, whose baritone voice and songs of hardship, redemption, and outlaw swagger made him one of the most influential figures in American music across six decades.

02-26.title: Napoleon Escapes from Elba
02-26.description: Napoleon Bonaparte slipped past his guards and sailed from the island of Elba with 700 men, landing in southern France to begin the Hundred Days campaign that ended at Waterloo.

02-26.title: Thriller Hits Number One
02-26.description: Michael Jackson's Thriller topped the Billboard Album chart, eventually spending 37 non-consecutive weeks at number one and becoming the best-selling album in history with over 70 million copies sold.

02-26.title: Thriller — Michael Jackson
02-26.description: Michael Jackson's genre-defining album produced seven top-ten singles, won eight Grammy Awards, and sold over 70 million copies to become the best-selling album of all time.

02-26.title: Les Misérables
02-26.description: Tom Hooper's emotionally overwhelming musical adaptation of Victor Hugo's novel featured Anne Hathaway's Oscar-winning performance of I Dreamed a Dream, recorded in one raw live take.

02-27.title: Elizabeth Taylor
02-27.description: Hollywood legend who won two Academy Awards and captivated the world with her violet eyes, extraordinary beauty, and turbulent off-screen life that became a mirror of celebrity culture.

02-27.title: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
02-27.description: The most widely read American poet of the 19th century, whose narrative poems Paul Revere's Ride and The Song of Hiawatha shaped how Americans imagined their own history.

02-27.title: Joaquin Phoenix
02-27.description: Intense and transformative actor who won the Academy Award for Best Actor for Joker and delivered acclaimed performances in Walk the Line, Gladiator, and The Master.

02-27.title: Lincoln's Cooper Union Speech
02-27.description: Abraham Lincoln delivered a masterful speech at New York's Cooper Union arguing against slavery's expansion, a performance so powerful it essentially launched his presidential campaign.

02-27.title: 19th Amendment Upheld
02-27.description: The U.S. Supreme Court unanimously upheld the constitutionality of the 19th Amendment in Leser v. Garnett, definitively protecting women's right to vote across all states.

02-27.title: Jagged Little Pill — Alanis Morissette
02-27.description: Alanis Morissette's raw and furious debut made her the youngest artist to win the Grammy for Album of the Year, and its 33 million copies sold made it one of the decade's biggest records.

02-27.title: Walk the Line
02-27.description: James Mangold's biography of Johnny Cash starred Joaquin Phoenix and Reese Witherspoon in Oscar-winning performances that captured the magnetic tension between Cash and June Carter.

02-28.title: Linus Pauling
02-28.description: American chemist who won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry and the Nobel Peace Prize, one of very few people to win two Nobel Prizes, for pioneering quantum chemistry and campaigning against nuclear testing.

02-28.title: Brian Jones
02-28.description: Multi-instrumentalist founder of the Rolling Stones who brought blues authenticity and musical experimentation to the band before his tragic death at 27 in 1969.

02-28.title: Jason Aldean
02-28.description: Country music superstar whose rock-influenced sound helped define the new era of stadium country, producing chart-topping albums over two decades of relentless touring.

02-28.title: U2 Releases War
02-28.description: U2 released their politically charged third album, which knocked Michael Jackson's Thriller from the top of the UK charts and became the Irish band's first number-one album.

02-28.title: Michael Jackson Wins 8 Grammys
02-28.description: At the 26th Grammy Awards, Michael Jackson took home a record-breaking eight awards in a single night for the Thriller album, a record that still stands.

02-28.title: War — U2
02-28.description: U2's urgent political album, featuring Sunday Bloody Sunday and New Year's Day, announced the band as one of the most important voices in rock and roll with its passionate moral clarity.

02-28.title: Pretty in Pink
02-28.description: John Hughes's tender class-divide romance starred Molly Ringwald as a working-class girl navigating the social minefield of high school in a film that defined the 1980s teen drama.

02-29.title: Gioachino Rossini
02-29.description: Italian opera master born on Leap Day who composed The Barber of Seville and William Tell in a career of dazzling comic and dramatic genius before retiring at only 37.

02-29.title: Dinah Shore
02-29.description: Pioneering American singer and television personality who became one of the first major female solo artists in American music and hosted one of the longest-running TV variety shows.

02-29.title: Ja Rule
02-29.description: New York rapper whose melodic style and string of collaborations with Jennifer Lopez and Ashanti made him one of the dominant hip-hop voices of the early 2000s.

02-29.title: Salem Witch Trials Begin
02-29.description: The first warrants were issued in the Salem witch trials, setting in motion a mass hysteria that would lead to the execution of twenty people in colonial Massachusetts.

02-29.title: Hattie McDaniel Wins Oscar
02-29.description: Hattie McDaniel became the first African American to win an Academy Award, claiming Best Supporting Actress for Gone with the Wind, though she was seated separately from her white co-stars.

02-29.title: Come Fly with Me — Frank Sinatra
02-29.description: Frank Sinatra's swinging travelogue album began a five-week run atop the Billboard 200 on this Leap Day, its Nelson Riddle arrangements perfectly capturing postwar optimism.

02-29.title: The Return of the King
02-29.description: On Leap Day 2004, Peter Jackson's epic conclusion to The Lord of the Rings swept the Academy Awards, winning all 11 Oscars for which it was nominated, tying the all-time record.
